#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resolution-rate summary for harbor job dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--family LABEL] [--expected-trials N] [--model M]
               [--fa-ref REF] [--run-url URL] <jobs-dir>

Reads <jobs-dir>/<job>/*/result.json (per-trial TrialResults; each job's
top-level result.json is a file, not a dir, so the glob skips it) and
prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown resolution table, also appending it to
$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

--family (bench-harbor.yml passes it; issue #1124) keys the report to one
Terminal-Bench dataset family: jobs are read from fa-<family>-<env>-gpu-*
for the GPU split (everything else under the same prefix is CPU) and job
dirs from OTHER families are ignored — merged artifacts from different
dataset versions never cross-contaminate a report. Without --family the
legacy behaviour applies (all job dirs; fa-4.0-* naming; title pinned to
4.0).

With --family the report ends in a paste-ready row for the per-version
results ledger in docs/bench.md (dataset, model, fa commit, date,
resolution, run — cost column stays "—" until the token card lands).

A trial is resolved when every verifier reward is 1.0; the resolution rate
is resolved trials / attempted trials. harbor exits 0 even with unresolved
trials, so the exit code is the verdict on run COMPLETENESS only: 1 when
nothing was produced or fewer than --expected-trials trials were attempted
(lost shard). Unresolved trials are the scoreboard, not an infra failure —
reported without failing the step.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import families


def _trial_rows(job_dir: Path) -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(str(job_dir / "*" / "result.json"))):
        data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
        rewards = (data.get("verifier_result") or {}).get("rewards") or {}
        scores = [float(v) for v in rewards.values()]
        resolved = bool(scores) and all(v >= 1.0 for v in scores)
        exception = (data.get("exception_info") or {}).get("exception_type") or ""
        rows.append({"resolved": resolved, "exception": exception})
    return rows


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("jobs_dir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-trials", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--family",
        choices=sorted(families.FAMILIES),
        default=None,
        help="Terminal-Bench family label; keys the report to fa-<family>-* jobs",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=None, help="Model id for the ledger row")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-ref", dest="fa_ref", default=None, help="fa commit for the ledger row")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_url", default=None, help="Workflow run url for the ledger row")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    prefix = f"fa-{args.family}-" if args.family else None
    splits: dict[str, list[dict]] = {"cpu": [], "gpu": []}
    job_dirs = [
        d for d in sorted(args.jobs_dir.glob("*"))
        if d.is_dir() and (prefix is None or d.name.startswith(prefix))
    ]
    for job_dir in job_dirs:
        name = job_dir.name
        if "-gpu-" in name:
            split = "gpu"
        elif "-cpu-" in name:
            split = "cpu"
        else:
            # legacy scheme: docker shards were CPU, modal was the GPU leg
            split = "gpu" if "modal" in name else "cpu"
        splits[split].extend(_trial_rows(job_dir))

    title = (
        f"### fa on Terminal-Bench {args.family} ({families.FAMILIES[args.family]})"
        if args.family
        else "### fa on Terminal-Bench 4.0"
    )
    lines = [title, ""]
    problems: list[str] = []
    total_resolved = total_rows = 0

    if not job_dirs:
        lines.append("**No harbor jobs found — the run did not complete.**")
        problems.append("no harbor jobs found")
    else:
        table = ["| split | resolved | rate |", "|---|---|---|"]
        for split, label in (("cpu", "CPU shards"), ("gpu", "GPU shards")):
            rows = splits[split]
            if not rows:
                table.append(f"| {label} | 0/0 | no trials |")
                continue
            scored = [r for r in rows if not r["exception"]]
            errored = len(rows) - len(scored)
            resolved = sum(1 for r in scored if r["resolved"])
            total_resolved += resolved
            total_rows += len(scored)
            note = f"{errored} errored" if errored else f"{resolved / len(scored):.1%}"
            table.append(f"| {label} | {resolved}/{len(scored)} | {note} |")
        lines.append(f"**Resolution: {total_resolved}/{total_rows} scored trials**")
        lines.append("")
        lines.extend(table)

        exceptions: dict[str, int] = {}
        for rows in splits.values():
            for r in rows:
                if r["exception"]:
                    exceptions[r["exception"]] = exceptions.get(r["exception"], 0) + 1
        if exceptions:
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(
                "Errored trials (harness/infra failure, not scored): "
                + ", ".join(f"{k} ×{v}" for k, v in sorted(exceptions.items()))
            )
            problems.append(
                f"{sum(exceptions.values())} trial(s) errored before producing a verdict"
            )

        expected = args.expected_trials
        if expected is not None and total_rows < expected:
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(
                f"**Incomplete run: {total_rows}/{expected} expected trials attempted"
                " (lost or timed-out shard).**"
            )
            problems.append(f"only {total_rows}/{expected} expected trials attempted")

    if args.family and total_rows:
        rate = f"{total_resolved / total_rows:.1%}" if total_rows else "—"
        today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        lines.extend([
            "",
            "### Ledger row — append to docs/bench.md (rows are append-only)",
            "",
            "| dataset | model | fa | date | resolution | cost | run |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
            f"| {families.FAMILIES[args.family]} | {args.model or '—'} "
            f"| {args.fa_ref or '—'} | {today} "
            f"| {total_resolved}/{total_rows} trials ({rate}) "
            f"| — (token card pending) | {args.run_url or '—'} |",
        ])

    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"):
        with open(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"], "a") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    else:
        print("\n".join(lines))

    return 0 if not problems else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Split a downloaded harbor dataset into CPU and GPU task shards.

Usage:
    split_tasks.py <dataset-dir> [--filter <glob>[,<glob>...]] [--shards N]
                   [--cpu-env ENV] [--task-prefix PREFIX]

Scans every <dataset-dir>/*/task.toml for a `gpus > 0` declaration.
CPU tasks (gpus == 0 or absent) are chunked into `--shards` shards on the
env given by --cpu-env (default `modal`: the issue's own command uses
`-e modal` and the self-hosted runner mac has no docker; pass docker once
the runner gains it). GPU tasks always go on modal — the GPU split rides
the same matrix as a shard with env=modal.

harbor's `-i` filter matches fully-qualified task ids (`<org>/<name>`, as
`get_name()` reports them), so --task-prefix (e.g. `terminal-bench/`, the
org part of the dataset spec) is prepended to every emitted task name.

With --shards, writes the workflow matrix to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (or stdout):
    matrix={"include": [{"i": 0, "env": "modal", "tasks": "a b c"}, ...,
                        {"i": N,   "env": "modal",  "tasks": "gpu1 gpu2"}]}
    count=... cpu_count=... gpu_count=...

Without it, prints the plain split (CPU_TASKS=... GPU_TASKS=... counts).
`--filter` (comma fnmatch globs on task names) narrows both lists — the
smoke path passes one task name and gets a single-task shard.
"""
import argparse
import fnmatch
import json
import os
import sys
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path


def _max_gpus(obj) -> int:
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        best = 0
        for key, value in obj.items():
            if key == "gpus" and isinstance(value, int):
                best = max(best, value)
            else:
                best = max(best, _max_gpus(value))
        return best
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        return max((_max_gpus(v) for v in obj), default=0)
    return 0


def _split(dataset_dir: Path, globs: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    cpu: list[str] = []
    gpu: list[str] = []
    for task_dir in sorted(dataset_dir.iterdir()):
        task_toml = task_dir / "task.toml"
        if not task_toml.is_file():
            continue
        name = task_dir.name
        if globs and not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, g) for g in globs):
            continue
        config = tomllib.loads(task_toml.read_text())
        (gpu if _max_gpus(config) > 0 else cpu).append(name)
    return cpu, gpu


def _chunk(tasks: list[str], shards: int) -> list[list[str]]:
    shards = max(1, min(shards, len(tasks) or 1))
    size, extra = divmod(len(tasks), shards)
    out, at = [], 0
    for i in range(shards):
        end = at + size + (1 if i < extra else 0)
        out.append(tasks[at:end])
        at = end
    return out


def _emit(pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
    target = os.environ.get("GITHUB_OUTPUT")
    if target:
        with open(target, "a") as f:
            f.writelines(f"{k}={v}\n" for k, v in pairs)
    else:
        for k, v in pairs:
            print(f"{k}={v}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("dataset_dir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--filter", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--shards", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--cpu-env", default="modal")
    parser.add_argument("--task-prefix", default="")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    globs = [g.strip() for g in args.filter.split(",") if g.strip()]
    cpu, gpu = _split(args.dataset_dir, globs)
    if not cpu and not gpu:
        print("no tasks matched", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if not args.shards:
        print(f'CPU_TASKS="{" ".join(cpu)}"')
        print(f'GPU_TASKS="{" ".join(gpu)}"')
        print(f"CPU_COUNT={len(cpu)}")
        print(f"GPU_COUNT={len(gpu)}")
        return 0

    include = [
        {
            "i": i,
            "env": args.cpu_env,
            "kind": "cpu",
            "tasks": " ".join(args.task_prefix + t for t in chunk),
        }
        for i, chunk in enumerate(_chunk(cpu, args.shards))
        if chunk
    ]
    if gpu:
        include.append(
            {
                "i": len(include),
                "env": "modal",
                "kind": "gpu",
                "tasks": " ".join(args.task_prefix + t for t in gpu),
            }
        )
    _emit(
        [
            ("matrix", json.dumps({"include": include})),
            ("count", str(len(cpu) + len(gpu))),
            ("cpu_count", str(len(cpu))),
            ("gpu_count", str(len(gpu))),
        ]
    )
    print(
        f"{len(cpu)} CPU task(s) across {len(include) - (1 if gpu else 0)}"
        f" {args.cpu_env} shard(s), {len(gpu)} GPU task(s) on modal"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

name: Bench 4.0

# Runs the fa coding agent against Terminal-Bench 4.0 on the Harbor
# framework (issue #147): all shards run via Modal sandboxes by default
# (the issue's own command uses -e modal; the self-hosted runner mac has
# no docker), with cpu-env=docker available once the runner gains docker.
# Results upload to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source
# (tbench.ai). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives in
# bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (e.g. hello-world for smoke; empty = full 66-task dataset)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Harbor dataset spec'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0'
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (modal default; docker once the self-hosted runner has it)'
        required: false
        default: 'modal'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (it orchestrates Modal sandboxes; needs docker only with cpu-env=docker)'
        required: false
        default: 'self-hosted'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench-4.0
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run.
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench 4.0, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ inputs.model }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench 4.0 agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot write the
      # hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the runner's
      # own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14. Get a
      # uv-managed CPython 3.13 in user space instead (no admin, no tool
      # cache); uv is also the canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}'
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ inputs.model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ -n "$FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI" ] || { echo '::error::FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY secret is not set'; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-mask…

Very minor; the ledger's purpose is pinning @latest content. Not worth a comment? Possibly a small SUGGESTION. I'll fold into a suggestion comment about ledger metadata.

- **PR #**: 1128
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1128
- **Title**: feat(#1124): Terminal-Bench family coverage 2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0 from one dispatch surface
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1124` → `main`
- **State**: open

- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T20:56:14Z

## PR Description

Closes #1124

## What

The Harbor bench dispatch now runs the **whole Terminal-Bench dataset family from one surface** — no per-family bespoke entry points:

| family | Harbor dataset id | tasks | smoke task |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2@latest` | 89 | `fix-git` |
| 2.1 | `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` | 89 | `fix-git` |
| 3.0 | `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@3.0.0` | 74 | `bun-sourcemap-leak` |
| 4.0 | `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0` | 66 | `bun-sourcemap-leak` |

### OQ1 resolved — exact Harbor dataset ids (verified against the Harbor Hub registry, 2026-09-30)

The card's assumption ("version tags on the same dataset slug") is **wrong for 2.x**. harbor resolves `<org>/<name>@<ref>` through the Hub's **tag table**:

- `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0` → tag `4.0.0` (serves content v3.0.1) — the live leaderboard dataset ✔ (also `@3.0.0` → v1.0.0 content, `@latest`, `@4.0.0-rc1/rc2`)
- Terminal-Bench **2.0** and **2.1** live under **separate package names**: `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2` and `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1`, whose only tag is `latest` (2.0 = 89 tasks; 2.1 = same 89-task set with `install-windows-3-11` renamed to `install-windows-3.11`; 3.0 = 74 tasks, 4.0 = 66 — counts read from the Hub).
- `@latest` is mutable: the resolved content hash appears in the harbor download log; the ledger row's run date pins the set.

`bench/harbor_fa/families.py` pins the verified ids and resolves every accepted input form (label `2.1`, bare `4.0.0`/`v4`, full id).

## Dispatch surface — before / after

**Before** (`Bench 4.0` / `bench-4.0.yml`): `dataset` free-text, default `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; job names/artifacts/summary hardcoded `4.0`; a typo'd dataset died deep in the shard step or silently mis-keyed results; no unit tests for the harbor bench scripts.

**After** (`Bench Harbor` / `bench-harbor.yml`): same file-shape, one added input, one added setup step —
- setup: **Resolve Terminal-Bench family** — `families.py resolve "$DATASET"` emits `family=` / `dataset=` / `smoke=`; unknown, out-of-family, or version-less specs fail fast with a `::error::` naming the spec and all known ids (**E1**, never a silent fallback to 4.0). The unit-test step now gates the setup job (`python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa`), same as `bench.yml` gates the legacy scripts.
- setup: **Confirm full intermediate-family run** — full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 require `confirm-full-run: true` (**E3** cost guard); smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected.
- bench: harbor jobs named `fa-<family>-<env>-<kind>-<shard>` (`fa-4.0-*` byte-identical to today), Hub upload globs `jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*`.
- summary: keyed per family (`fa-<family>-*` jobs only — merged artifacts from different dataset versions **cannot cross-contaminate** a report), title names the family + resolved id, and ends in a paste-ready ledger row.
- concurrency group `bench-4.0` → `bench-harbor` (serializes family-wide).

## Per-version results ledger (AC3)

`docs/bench.md` gains an **append-only** per-version table (dataset, model, fa commit, date, resolution, cost, run); each run's job summary ends in a copy-paste row for it:

```markdown
### Ledger row — append to docs/bench.md (rows are append-only)

| dataset | model | fa | date | resolution | cost | run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest | glm-5.3-flash | abc1234 | 2026-09-30 | 1/1 trials (100.0%) | — (token card pending) | https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/1 |
```

AC4 (default-dispatch parity): default input, dataset id, harbor invocation, job names (`fa-4.0-…`), artifact names and Hub uploads are unchanged; the summary gains the family title suffix + ledger block (additive). Cost column stays `—` until the token/cost card (#1123) lands; timeout caps stay flat until #1122 (E2, per card).

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` — 18 tests OK (family ids pinned to the Hub-verified values; each family resolves; unknown/version-less/out-of-family error loudly via CLI subprocess; ledger separation proves a `fa-4.0-*` dir in a 2.1 report is excluded; legacy no-`--family` invocation unchanged). Legacy suite `bench/terminal_bench` — 15 tests OK.
- Workflow YAML parse-checked; `families.py resolve` exercised for every family and every input form.
- No Dart code touched — nothing to analyze; adapter (`fa_agent.py`) untouched per the card's "datasets are inputs, not code paths" invariant.

## Notes for the CI owner (rename heads-up)

Workflow file `bench-4.0.yml` → `bench-harbor.yml` (name `Bench 4.0` → `Bench Harbor`), per the card's "rename/generalize the Harbor workflow dispatch" contract. If the SM bench queue keys on the old workflow name/file, it needs the new one. No CI dispatch is performed or requested by this PR.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Terminal-Bench family manifest for the Harbor bench surface (issue #1124).
+
+One dispatch surface (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`) runs every live
+Terminal-Bench dataset family next to the legacy 0.1.1 regression set
+(`bench.yml`, tb CLI — board closed):
+
+    family  harbor dataset id                            tasks  smoke
+    ------  -------------------------------------------  -----  ------------------
+    2.0     terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2@latest       89     fix-git
+    2.1     terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest     89     fix-git
+    3.0     terminal-bench/terminal-bench@3.0.0          74     bun-sourcemap-leak
+    4.0     terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0          66     bun-sourcemap-leak
+
+Ids verified against the Harbor Hub registry on 2026-09-30 (issue OQ1):
+harbor resolves `<org>/<name>@<ref>` through the Hub's tag table — the
+`terminal-bench` package tags `4.0.0` (content v3.0.1) and `3.0.0` carry
+the 4.0/3.0 datasets, while the 2.x sets live under separate package
+names (`terminal-bench-2`, `terminal-bench-2-1`) whose only tag is
+`latest`. `@latest` is mutable; a ledger row's run date pins it (the
+resolved content hash appears in the harbor download log).
+
+Usage (workflow setup step):
+
+    families.py resolve DATASET
+
+DATASET is a family label (`2.1`), a bare version (`4.0.0`, `v4`), or a
+full Harbor dataset id (`terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`). Emits
+`family=` / `dataset=` / `smoke=` to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (or stdout). An
+unknown, out-of-family, or version-less spec fails loudly on stderr with
+a `::error::` annotation and exit 1 — never a silent fallback to 4.0.
+"""
+import argparse
+import os
+import sys
+
+# family label -> canonical Harbor dataset id (see module docstring, OQ1).
+FAMILIES = {
+    "2.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2@latest",
+    "2.1": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest",
+    "3.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@3.0.0",
+    "4.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0",
+}
+
+# One-task smoke per family (verified present in each dataset's task set);
+# dispatch with tasks=<smoke>, attempts=1 before any full run.
+SMOKE_TASKS = {
+    "2.0": "fix-git",
+    "2.1": "fix-git",
+    "3.0": "bun-sourcemap-leak",
+    "4.0": "bun-sourcemap-leak",
+}
+
+# Task count per family (Harbor Hub, 2026-09-30) — shard-count guidance in
+# docs/bench.md scales on these.
+TASK_COUNTS = {
+    "2.0": 89,
+    "2.1": 89,
+    "3.0": 74,
+    "4.0": 66,
+}
+
+
+class FamilyError(ValueError):
+    """Dataset spec is not part of the pinned Terminal-Bench family."""
+
+
+def _known_ids() -> str:
+    return ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in FAMILIES.items())
+
+
+def _normalize_label(text: str) -> str:
+    """'4.0.0' / 'v4.0' / '4' -> '4.0'; anything else raises FamilyError."""
+    t = text.strip().lower().removeprefix("v")
+    parts = t.split(".")
+    if not parts or not parts[0].isdigit():
+        raise FamilyError(f"'{text}' is not a Terminal-Bench family version")
+    major = parts[0]
+    minor = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 and parts[1].isdigit() else "0"
+    return f"{major}.{minor}"
+
+
+def resolve(spec: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    """Map a dataset input to (family label, canonical Harbor dataset id)."""
+    s = (spec or "").strip()
+    if s in FAMILIES:
+        return s, FAMILIES[s]
+    if "@" in s:
+        name, _, tag = s.partition("@")
+        try:
+            label = _normalize_label(tag)
+        except FamilyError:
+            label = None
+        if label and label in FAMILIES and FAMILIES[label] == s:
+            return label, s
+    else:
+        try:
+            label = _normalize_label(s)
+        except FamilyError:
+            label = None
+        if label and label in FAMILIES:
+            return label, FAMILIES[label]
+    raise FamilyError(
+        f"dataset spec '{spec}' is not part of the pinned Terminal-Bench "
+        f"family; pass a family label (2.0, 2.1, 3.0, 4.0) or one of the "
+        f"exact Harbor ids: {_known_ids()}. Version-less specs are rejected "
+        f"(no silent fallback to 4.0)."
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+    p_resolve = sub.add_parser("resolve", help="Resolve a dataset input")
+    p_resolve.add_argument("dataset", help="Family label, version, or full id")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    try:
+        family, dataset = resolve(args.dataset)
+    except FamilyError as e:
+        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    pairs = [
+        ("family", family),
+        ("dataset", dataset),
+        ("smoke", SMOKE_TASKS[family]),
+    ]
+    # Human-readable line for the run log (machine output goes to
+    # GITHUB_OUTPUT / stdout below).
+    print(
+        f"resolved: family={family} dataset={dataset} smoke={SMOKE_TASKS[family]}",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+    target = os.environ.get("GITHUB_OUTPUT")
+    if target:
+        with open(target, "a") as f:
+            f.writelines(f"{k}={v}\n" for k, v in pairs)
+    else:
+        for k, v in pairs:
+            print(f"{k}={v}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+

+
+class ManifestTest(unittest.TestCase):

+        # OQ1 (2026-09-30): 4.0/3.0 are tags on the terminal-bench package;
+        # the 2.x sets live under separate package names, whose only tag is
+        # 'latest'. A change here means the Hub moved — re-verify before
+        # editing.
+        self.assertEqual(FAMILIES, {
+            "2.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2@latest",
+            "2.1": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest",
+            "3.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@3.0.0",
+            "4.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0",
+        })
+

+        self.assertEqual(set(FAMILIES), set(SMOKE_TASKS))

+        for count in TASK_COUNTS.values():
+            self.assertGreater(count, 0)
+
+

+        self.assertEqual(

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resolution-rate summary for harbor job dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--family LABEL] [--expected-trials N] [--model M]
               [--fa-ref REF] [--run-url URL] <jobs-dir>

Reads <jobs-dir>/<job>/*/result.json (per-trial TrialResults; each job's
top-level result.json is a file, not a dir, so the glob skips it) and
prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown resolution table, also appending it to
$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

--family (bench-harbor.yml passes it; issue #1124) keys the report to one
Terminal-Bench dataset family: jobs are read from fa-<family>-<env>-gpu-*
for the GPU split (everything else under the same prefix is CPU) and job
dirs from OTHER families are ignored — merged artifacts from different
dataset versions never cross-contaminate a report. Without --family the
legacy behaviour applies (all job dirs; fa-4.0-* naming; title pinned to
4.0).

With --family the report ends in a paste-ready row for the per-version
results ledger in docs/bench.md (dataset, model, fa commit, date,
resolution, run — cost column stays "—" until the token card lands).

A trial is resolved when every verifier reward is 1.0; the resolution rate
is resolved trials / attempted trials. harbor exits 0 even with unresolved
trials, so the exit code is the verdict on run COMPLETENESS only: 1 when
nothing was produced or fewer than --expected-trials trials were attempted
(lost shard). Unresolved trials are the scoreboard, not an infra failure —
reported without failing the step.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import families


def _trial_rows(job_dir: Path) -> list[dict]:
    rows = []
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(str(job_dir / "*" / "result.json"))):
        data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
        rewards = (data.get("verifier_result") or {}).get("rewards") or {}
        scores = [float(v) for v in rewards.values()]
        resolved = bool(scores) and all(v >= 1.0 for v in scores)
        exception = (data.get("exception_info") or {}).get("exception_type") or ""
        rows.append({"resolved": resolved, "exception": exception})
    return rows


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("jobs_dir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--expected-trials", type=int, default=None)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--family",
        choices=sorted(families.FAMILIES),
        default=None,
        help="Terminal-Bench family label; keys the report to fa-<family>-* jobs",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=None, help="Model id for the ledger row")
    parser.add_argument("--fa-ref", dest="fa_ref", default=None, help="fa commit for the ledger row")
    parser.add_argument("--run-url", dest="run_url", default=None, help="Workflow run url for the ledger row")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    prefix = f"fa-{args.family}-" if args.family else None
    splits: dict[str, list[dict]] = {"cpu": [], "gpu": []}
    job_dirs = [
        d for d in sorted(args.jobs_dir.glob("*"))
        if d.is_dir() and (prefix is None or d.name.startswith(prefix))
    ]
    for job_dir in job_dirs:
        name = job_dir.name
        if "-gpu-" in name:
            split = "gpu"
        elif "-cpu-" in name:
            split = "cpu"
        else:
            # legacy scheme: docker shards were CPU, modal was the GPU leg
            split = "gpu" if "modal" in name else "cpu"
        splits[split].extend(_trial_rows(job_dir))

    title = (
        f"### fa on Terminal-Bench {args.family} ({families.FAMILIES[args.family]})"
        if args.family
        else "### fa on Terminal-Bench 4.0"
    )
    lines = [title, ""]
    problems: list[str] = []
    total_resolved = total_rows = 0

    if not job_dirs:
        lines.append("**No harbor jobs found — the run did not complete.**")
        problems.append("no harbor jobs found")
    else:
        table = ["| split | resolved | rate |", "|---|---|---|"]
        for split, label in (("cpu", "CPU shards"), ("gpu", "GPU shards")):
            rows = splits[split]
            if not rows:
                table.append(f"| {label} | 0/0 | no trials |")
                continue
            scored = [r for r in rows if not r["exception"]]
            errored = len(rows) - len(scored)
            resolved = sum(1 for r in scored if r["resolved"])
            total_resolved += resolved
            total_rows += len(scored)
            note = f"{errored} errored" if errored else f"{resolved / len(scored):.1%}"
            table.append(f"| {label} | {resolved}/{len(scored)} | {note} |")
        lines.append(f"**Resolution: {total_resolved}/{total_rows} scored trials**")
        lines.append("")
        lines.extend(table)

        exceptions: dict[str, int] = {}
        for rows in splits.values():
            for r in rows:
                if r["exception"]:
                    exceptions[r["exception"]] = exceptions.get(r["exception"], 0) + 1
        if exceptions:
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(
                "Errored trials (harness/infra failure, not scored): "
                + ", ".join(f"{k} ×{v}" for k, v in sorted(exceptions.items()))
            )
            problems.append(
                f"{sum(exceptions.values())} trial(s) errored before producing a verdict"
            )

        expected = args.expected_trials
        if expected is not None and total_rows < expected:
            lines.append("")
            lines.append(
                f"**Incomplete run: {total_rows}/{expected} expected trials attempted"
                " (lost or timed-out shard).**"
            )
            problems.append(f"only {total_rows}/{expected} expected trials attempted")

    if args.family and total_rows:
        rate = f"{total_resolved / total_rows:.1%}" if total_rows else "—"
        today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        lines.extend([
            "",
            "### Ledger row — append to docs/bench.md (rows are append-only)",
            "",
            "| dataset | model | fa | date | resolution | cost | run |",
            "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
            f"| {families.FAMILIES[args.family]} | {args.model or '—'} "
            f"| {args.fa_ref or '—'} | {today} "
            f"| {total_resolved}/{total_rows} trials ({rate}) "
            f"| — (token card pending) | {args.run_url or '—'} |",
        ])

    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"):
        with open(os.environ["GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"], "a") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    else:
        print("\n".join(lines))

    return 0 if not problems else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Split a downloaded harbor dataset into CPU and GPU task shards.

Usage:
    split_tasks.py <dataset-dir> [--filter <glob>[,<glob>...]] [--shards N]
                   [--cpu-env ENV] [--task-prefix PREFIX]

Scans every <dataset-dir>/*/task.toml for a `gpus > 0` declaration.
CPU tasks (gpus == 0 or absent) are chunked into `--shards` shards on the
env given by --cpu-env (default `modal`: the issue's own command uses
`-e modal` and the self-hosted runner mac has no docker; pass docker once
the runner gains it). GPU tasks always go on modal — the GPU split rides
the same matrix as a shard with env=modal.

harbor's `-i` filter matches fully-qualified task ids (`<org>/<name>`, as
`get_name()` reports them), so --task-prefix (e.g. `terminal-bench/`, the
org part of the dataset spec) is prepended to every emitted task name.

With --shards, writes the workflow matrix to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (or stdout):
    matrix={"include": [{"i": 0, "env": "modal", "tasks": "a b c"}, ...,
                        {"i": N,   "env": "modal",  "tasks": "gpu1 gpu2"}]}
    count=... cpu_count=... gpu_count=...

Without it, prints the plain split (CPU_TASKS=... GPU_TASKS=... counts).
`--filter` (comma fnmatch globs on task names) narrows both lists — the
smoke path passes one task name and gets a single-task shard.
"""
import argparse
import fnmatch
import json
import os
import sys
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path


def _max_gpus(obj) -> int:
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        best = 0
        for key, value in obj.items():
            if key == "gpus" and isinstance(value, int):
                best = max(best, value)
            else:
                best = max(best, _max_gpus(value))
        return best
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        return max((_max_gpus(v) for v in obj), default=0)
    return 0


def _split(dataset_dir: Path, globs: list[str]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
    cpu: list[str] = []
    gpu: list[str] = []
    for task_dir in sorted(dataset_dir.iterdir()):
        task_toml = task_dir / "task.toml"
        if not task_toml.is_file():
            continue
        name = task_dir.name
        if globs and not any(fnmatch.fnmatch(name, g) for g in globs):
            continue
        config = tomllib.loads(task_toml.read_text())
        (gpu if _max_gpus(config) > 0 else cpu).append(name)
    return cpu, gpu


def _chunk(tasks: list[str], shards: int) -> list[list[str]]:
    shards = max(1, min(shards, len(tasks) or 1))
    size, extra = divmod(len(tasks), shards)
    out, at = [], 0
    for i in range(shards):
        end = at + size + (1 if i < extra else 0)
        out.append(tasks[at:end])
        at = end
    return out


def _emit(pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]) -> None:
    target = os.environ.get("GITHUB_OUTPUT")
    if target:
        with open(target, "a") as f:
            f.writelines(f"{k}={v}\n" for k, v in pairs)
    else:
        for k, v in pairs:
            print(f"{k}={v}")


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("dataset_dir", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--filter", default="")
    parser.add_argument("--shards", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--cpu-env", default="modal")
    parser.add_argument("--task-prefix", default="")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    globs = [g.strip() for g in args.filter.split(",") if g.strip()]
    cpu, gpu = _split(args.dataset_dir, globs)
    if not cpu and not gpu:
        print("no tasks matched", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    if not args.shards:
        print(f'CPU_TASKS="{" ".join(cpu)}"')
        print(f'GPU_TASKS="{" ".join(gpu)}"')
        print(f"CPU_COUNT={len(cpu)}")
        print(f"GPU_COUNT={len(gpu)}")
        return 0

    include = [
        {
            "i": i,
            "env": args.cpu_env,
            "kind": "cpu",
            "tasks": " ".join(args.task_prefix + t for t in chunk),
        }
        for i, chunk in enumerate(_chunk(cpu, args.shards))
        if chunk
    ]
    if gpu:
        include.append(
            {
                "i": len(include),
                "env": "modal",
                "kind": "gpu",
                "tasks": " ".join(args.task_prefix + t for t in gpu),
            }
        )
    _emit(
        [
            ("matrix", json.dumps({"include": include})),
            ("count", str(len(cpu) + len(gpu))),
            ("cpu_count", str(len(cpu))),
            ("gpu_count", str(len(gpu))),
        ]
    )
    print(
        f"{len(cpu)} CPU task(s) across {len(include) - (1 if gpu else 0)}"
        f" {args.cpu_env} shard(s), {len(gpu)} GPU task(s) on modal"
    )
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

name: Bench 4.0

# Runs the fa coding agent against Terminal-Bench 4.0 on the Harbor
# framework (issue #147): all shards run via Modal sandboxes by default
# (the issue's own command uses -e modal; the self-hosted runner mac has
# no docker), with cpu-env=docker available once the runner gains docker.
# Results upload to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source
# (tbench.ai). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives in
# bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (e.g. hello-world for smoke; empty = full 66-task dataset)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Harbor dataset spec'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0'
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (modal default; docker once the self-hosted runner has it)'
        required: false
        default: 'modal'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (it orchestrates Modal sandboxes; needs docker only with cpu-env=docker)'
        required: false
        default: 'self-hosted'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench-4.0
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
      # into its own cache during the run.
      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
        id: shards
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
        run: |
          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
          # org part of the dataset spec.
          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
            --task-prefix "${DATASET%%/*}/"

  bench:
    name: fa on tbench 4.0, shard ${{ matrix.i }} (${{ matrix.env }}, ${{ inputs.model }})
    needs: setup
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.cpu-runner }}
    # ~4 tasks/shard x --n-attempts x task runtime (tbench 4.0 agent caps
    # reach 8h but typical runs are far shorter) with headroom; the
    # self-hosted runner has no 6h hosted-runner cap to trip over.
    timeout-minutes: 355
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      max-parallel: 5
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.setup.outputs.matrix) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - name: Download fa bundle
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle

      # The self-hosted runner is a macOS box: setup-python cannot write the
      # hosted tool cache there (mkdir /Users/runner denied) and the runner's
      # own python3 is 3.14 — typer-based CLIs (harbor) break on 3.14. Get a
      # uv-managed CPython 3.13 in user space instead (no admin, no tool
      # cache); uv is also the canonical harbor install per the 4.0 docs.
      - name: Install harbor (uv-managed python 3.13)
        run: |
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          command -v uv >/dev/null || curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
          export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          uv venv --python 3.13 .bench-venv
          uv pip install --python .bench-venv/bin/python 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
          .bench-venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; print("venv python:", sys.version.split()[0])'

      - name: Run harbor (fa agent, ${{ matrix.env }} env)
        env:
          FA_BUNDLE_TARBALL: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-bundle.tar.gz
          PYTHONPATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/bench/harbor_fa
          FA_PROVIDER_TYPE: zai
          FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG: '{"baseUrl":"https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4","model":"glm-5.3-flash","apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI"}'
          FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_ID: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_ID }}
          MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET: ${{ secrets.MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET }}
          HARBOR_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.HARBOR_API_KEY }}
          MODEL: ${{ inputs.model }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
          NCONC: ${{ inputs.n-concurrent }}
          ENV_TYPE: ${{ matrix.env }}
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
          # shard task names: dataset dir names, no whitespace — safe to word-split.
          SHARD_TASKS: ${{ matrix.tasks }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          [ -n "$FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI" ] || { echo '::error::FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY secret is not set'; exit 1; }
          if [ "$ENV_TYPE" = modal ]; then
            [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_ID" ] && [ -n "$MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET" ] || { echo '::error::Modal secrets are not set'; exit 1; }
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded; GitHub
          # auto-mask…

Very minor; the ledger's purpose is pinning @latest content. Not worth a comment? Possibly a small SUGGESTION. I'll fold into a suggestion comment about ledger metadata.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Updated**: 2026-09-30T20:56:14Z

## PR Description

Closes #1124

## What

The Harbor bench dispatch now runs the **whole Terminal-Bench dataset family from one surface** — no per-family bespoke entry points:

| family | Harbor dataset id | tasks | smoke task |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.0 | `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2@latest` | 89 | `fix-git` |
| 2.1 | `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` | 89 | `fix-git` |
| 3.0 | `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@3.0.0` | 74 | `bun-sourcemap-leak` |
| 4.0 | `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0` | 66 | `bun-sourcemap-leak` |

### OQ1 resolved — exact Harbor dataset ids (verified against the Harbor Hub registry, 2026-09-30)

The card's assumption ("version tags on the same dataset slug") is **wrong for 2.x**. harbor resolves `<org>/<name>@<ref>` through the Hub's **tag table**:

- `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0` → tag `4.0.0` (serves content v3.0.1) — the live leaderboard dataset ✔ (also `@3.0.0` → v1.0.0 content, `@latest`, `@4.0.0-rc1/rc2`)
- Terminal-Bench **2.0** and **2.1** live under **separate package names**: `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2` and `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1`, whose only tag is `latest` (2.0 = 89 tasks; 2.1 = same 89-task set with `install-windows-3-11` renamed to `install-windows-3.11`; 3.0 = 74 tasks, 4.0 = 66 — counts read from the Hub).
- `@latest` is mutable: the resolved content hash appears in the harbor download log; the ledger row's run date pins the set.

`bench/harbor_fa/families.py` pins the verified ids and resolves every accepted input form (label `2.1`, bare `4.0.0`/`v4`, full id).

## Dispatch surface — before / after

**Before** (`Bench 4.0` / `bench-4.0.yml`): `dataset` free-text, default `terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`; job names/artifacts/summary hardcoded `4.0`; a typo'd dataset died deep in the shard step or silently mis-keyed results; no unit tests for the harbor bench scripts.

**After** (`Bench Harbor` / `bench-harbor.yml`): same file-shape, one added input, one added setup step —
- setup: **Resolve Terminal-Bench family** — `families.py resolve "$DATASET"` emits `family=` / `dataset=` / `smoke=`; unknown, out-of-family, or version-less specs fail fast with a `::error::` naming the spec and all known ids (**E1**, never a silent fallback to 4.0). The unit-test step now gates the setup job (`python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa`), same as `bench.yml` gates the legacy scripts.
- setup: **Confirm full intermediate-family run** — full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 require `confirm-full-run: true` (**E3** cost guard); smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected.
- bench: harbor jobs named `fa-<family>-<env>-<kind>-<shard>` (`fa-4.0-*` byte-identical to today), Hub upload globs `jobs/fa-${FAMILY}-*`.
- summary: keyed per family (`fa-<family>-*` jobs only — merged artifacts from different dataset versions **cannot cross-contaminate** a report), title names the family + resolved id, and ends in a paste-ready ledger row.
- concurrency group `bench-4.0` → `bench-harbor` (serializes family-wide).

## Per-version results ledger (AC3)

`docs/bench.md` gains an **append-only** per-version table (dataset, model, fa commit, date, resolution, cost, run); each run's job summary ends in a copy-paste row for it:

```markdown
### Ledger row — append to docs/bench.md (rows are append-only)

| dataset | model | fa | date | resolution | cost | run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest | glm-5.3-flash | abc1234 | 2026-09-30 | 1/1 trials (100.0%) | — (token card pending) | https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/actions/runs/1 |
```

AC4 (default-dispatch parity): default input, dataset id, harbor invocation, job names (`fa-4.0-…`), artifact names and Hub uploads are unchanged; the summary gains the family title suffix + ledger block (additive). Cost column stays `—` until the token/cost card (#1123) lands; timeout caps stay flat until #1122 (E2, per card).

## Verification

- `python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa` — 18 tests OK (family ids pinned to the Hub-verified values; each family resolves; unknown/version-less/out-of-family error loudly via CLI subprocess; ledger separation proves a `fa-4.0-*` dir in a 2.1 report is excluded; legacy no-`--family` invocation unchanged). Legacy suite `bench/terminal_bench` — 15 tests OK.
- Workflow YAML parse-checked; `families.py resolve` exercised for every family and every input form.
- No Dart code touched — nothing to analyze; adapter (`fa_agent.py`) untouched per the card's "datasets are inputs, not code paths" invariant.

## Notes for the CI owner (rename heads-up)

Workflow file `bench-4.0.yml` → `bench-harbor.yml` (name `Bench 4.0` → `Bench Harbor`), per the card's "rename/generalize the Harbor workflow dispatch" contract. If the SM bench queue keys on the old workflow name/file, it needs the new one. No CI dispatch is performed or requested by this PR.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Terminal-Bench family manifest for the Harbor bench surface (issue #1124).
+
+One dispatch surface (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml`) runs every live
+Terminal-Bench dataset family next to the legacy 0.1.1 regression set
+(`bench.yml`, tb CLI — board closed):
+
+    family  harbor dataset id                            tasks  smoke
+    ------  -------------------------------------------  -----  ------------------
+    2.0     terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2@latest       89     fix-git
+    2.1     terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest     89     fix-git
+    3.0     terminal-bench/terminal-bench@3.0.0          74     bun-sourcemap-leak
+    4.0     terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0          66     bun-sourcemap-leak
+
+Ids verified against the Harbor Hub registry on 2026-09-30 (issue OQ1):
+harbor resolves `<org>/<name>@<ref>` through the Hub's tag table — the
+`terminal-bench` package tags `4.0.0` (content v3.0.1) and `3.0.0` carry
+the 4.0/3.0 datasets, while the 2.x sets live under separate package
+names (`terminal-bench-2`, `terminal-bench-2-1`) whose only tag is
+`latest`. `@latest` is mutable; a ledger row's run date pins it (the
+resolved content hash appears in the harbor download log).
+
+Usage (workflow setup step):
+
+    families.py resolve DATASET
+
+DATASET is a family label (`2.1`), a bare version (`4.0.0`, `v4`), or a
+full Harbor dataset id (`terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0`). Emits
+`family=` / `dataset=` / `smoke=` to $GITHUB_OUTPUT (or stdout). An
+unknown, out-of-family, or version-less spec fails loudly on stderr with
+a `::error::` annotation and exit 1 — never a silent fallback to 4.0.
+"""
+import argparse
+import os
+import sys
+
+# family label -> canonical Harbor dataset id (see module docstring, OQ1).
+FAMILIES = {
+    "2.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2@latest",
+    "2.1": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest",
+    "3.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@3.0.0",
+    "4.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0",
+}
+
+# One-task smoke per family (verified present in each dataset's task set);
+# dispatch with tasks=<smoke>, attempts=1 before any full run.
+SMOKE_TASKS = {
+    "2.0": "fix-git",
+    "2.1": "fix-git",
+    "3.0": "bun-sourcemap-leak",
+    "4.0": "bun-sourcemap-leak",
+}
+
+# Task count per family (Harbor Hub, 2026-09-30) — shard-count guidance in
+# docs/bench.md scales on these.
+TASK_COUNTS = {
+    "2.0": 89,
+    "2.1": 89,
+    "3.0": 74,
+    "4.0": 66,
+}
+
+
+class FamilyError(ValueError):
+    """Dataset spec is not part of the pinned Terminal-Bench family."""
+
+
+def _known_ids() -> str:
+    return ", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in FAMILIES.items())
+
+
+def _normalize_label(text: str) -> str:
+    """'4.0.0' / 'v4.0' / '4' -> '4.0'; anything else raises FamilyError."""
+    t = text.strip().lower().removeprefix("v")
+    parts = t.split(".")
+    if not parts or not parts[0].isdigit():
+        raise FamilyError(f"'{text}' is not a Terminal-Bench family version")
+    major = parts[0]
+    minor = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 and parts[1].isdigit() else "0"
+    return f"{major}.{minor}"
+
+
+def resolve(spec: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
+    """Map a dataset input to (family label, canonical Harbor dataset id)."""
+    s = (spec or "").strip()
+    if s in FAMILIES:
+        return s, FAMILIES[s]
+    if "@" in s:
+        name, _, tag = s.partition("@")
+        try:
+            label = _normalize_label(tag)
+        except FamilyError:
+            label = None
+        if label and label in FAMILIES and FAMILIES[label] == s:
+            return label, s
+    else:
+        try:
+            label = _normalize_label(s)
+        except FamilyError:
+            label = None
+        if label and label in FAMILIES:
+            return label, FAMILIES[label]
+    raise FamilyError(
+        f"dataset spec '{spec}' is not part of the pinned Terminal-Bench "
+        f"family; pass a family label (2.0, 2.1, 3.0, 4.0) or one of the "
+        f"exact Harbor ids: {_known_ids()}. Version-less specs are rejected "
+        f"(no silent fallback to 4.0)."
+    )
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
+    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
+    p_resolve = sub.add_parser("resolve", help="Resolve a dataset input")
+    p_resolve.add_argument("dataset", help="Family label, version, or full id")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    try:
+        family, dataset = resolve(args.dataset)
+    except FamilyError as e:
+        print(f"::error::{e}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+
+    pairs = [
+        ("family", family),
+        ("dataset", dataset),
+        ("smoke", SMOKE_TASKS[family]),
+    ]
+    # Human-readable line for the run log (machine output goes to
+    # GITHUB_OUTPUT / stdout below).
+    print(
+        f"resolved: family={family} dataset={dataset} smoke={SMOKE_TASKS[family]}",
+        file=sys.stderr,
+    )
+    target = os.environ.get("GITHUB_OUTPUT")
+    if target:
+        with open(target, "a") as f:
+            f.writelines(f"{k}={v}\n" for k, v in pairs)
+    else:
+        for k, v in pairs:
+            print(f"{k}={v}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Unit tests for families.py (issue #1124). Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa"""
+import os
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from families import FAMILIES, SMOKE_TASKS, TASK_COUNTS, FamilyError, resolve
+
+SCRIPT = str(Path(__file__).parent / "families.py")
+
+
+class ManifestTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_ids_verified_against_harbor_hub(self):
+        # OQ1 (2026-09-30): 4.0/3.0 are tags on the terminal-bench package;
+        # the 2.x sets live under separate package names, whose only tag is
+        # 'latest'. A change here means the Hub moved — re-verify before
+        # editing.
+        self.assertEqual(FAMILIES, {
+            "2.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2@latest",
+            "2.1": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest",
+            "3.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@3.0.0",
+            "4.0": "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0",
+        })
+
+    def test_every_family_has_smoke_and_count(self):
+        self.assertEqual(set(FAMILIES), set(SMOKE_TASKS))
+        self.assertEqual(set(FAMILIES), set(TASK_COUNTS))
+        for count in TASK_COUNTS.values():
+            self.assertGreater(count, 0)
+
+
+class ResolveTest(unittest.TestCase):

+        for label, expected in FAMILIES.items():
+            self.assertEqual(resolve(label), (label, expected))
+
+    def test_full_id_and_bare_version_forms(self):
+        self.assertEqual(

+            ("4.0", "terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0"),
+        )

+        self.assertEqual(resolve("v2.1"), ("2.1", FAMILIES["2.1"]))
+        self.assertEqual(resolve("3"), ("3.0", FAMILIES["3.0"]))
+

+name: Bench Harbor
+
+# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
+# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
+# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
+# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
+# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
+# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback to 4.0). Shards run via Modal
+# sandboxes by default (the self-hosted runner mac has no docker), with
+# cpu-env=docker available once the runner gains docker. Results upload
+# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
+# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
+# in bench.yml.
+#
+# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
+# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
+# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
+# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
+#
+# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
+# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
+# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
+# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
+# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
+# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
+#
+# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
+#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
+#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
+#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
+#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      tasks:
+        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
+        required: false
+        default: ''
+      dataset:
+        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py)'
+        required: false
+        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench@4.0.0'
+      confirm-full-run:
+        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
+        required: false
+        type: boolean
+        default: false
+      model:
+        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
+        required: false
+        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
+      attempts:
+        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
+        required: false
+        default: '5'
+      n-concurrent:
+        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
+        required: false
+        default: '1'
+      shards:
+        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
+        required: false
+        default: '16'
+      cpu-env:
+        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (modal default; docker once the self-hosted runner has it)'
+        required: false
+        default: 'modal'
+      cpu-runner:
+        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (it orchestrates Modal sandboxes; needs docker only with cpu-env=docker)'
+        required: false
+        default: 'self-hosted'
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
+# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
+# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
+# back-to-back.
+concurrency:
+  group: bench-harbor
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  setup:
+    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    outputs:
+      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
+      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
+      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
+      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
+      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
+      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+
+      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
+      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
+        with:
+          sdk: stable
+
+      - run: dart pub get
+
+      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
+      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
+      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
+      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
+        id: family
+        env:
+          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
+        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"
+
+      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
+      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
+      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
+      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
+      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
+        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.tasks == '' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
+        run: |
+          echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
+          exit 1
+
+      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
+      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
+      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
+        run: |
+          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
+          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
+          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .
+
+      - name: Upload fa bundle
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          name: fa-bundle
+          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz
+
+      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
+      # break on 3.14.
+      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
+        with:
+          python-version: '3.13'
+
+      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
+      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'
+
+      # stdlib-only unit tests for the bench scripts; a manifest/shard bug
+      # costs a multi-hour run, so gate the surface on them (same as
+      # bench.yml gates the legacy scripts).
+      - name: Unit-test bench scripts
+        run: python -m unittest discover -s bench/harbor_fa -v
+
+      # Download the dataset once for classification; harbor re-fetches
+      # into its own cache during the run. DATASET is the canonical id
+      # resolved by the family step (the raw input may be a bare label).
+      - name: Shard dataset into CPU / GPU shards
+        id: shards
+        env:
+          DATASET: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
+          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
+          SHARDS: ${{ inputs.shards }}
+          CPU_ENV: ${{ inputs.cpu-env }}
+        run: |
+          harbor datasets download "$DATASET" --output-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/ds" --overwrite
+          # Dataset name at version: dir name is the dataset slug.
+          ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds/$(basename "${DATASET%%@*}")"
+          [ -d "$ds_dir" ] || ds_dir="$RUNNER_TEMP/ds"
+          # split_tasks.py writes the matrix/counts into GITHUB_OUTPUT itself.
+          # harbor -i matches qualified ids (<org>/<name>): prefix with the
+          # org part of the dataset spec.
+          python bench/harbor_fa/split_tasks.py "$ds_dir" \
+            --filter "$TASKS" --shards "$SHARDS" --cpu-env "$CPU_ENV" \
+    …
